newsitem.title: BAHRAIN: Bahrain says it contained unrest by individuals.
newsitem.headline: Bahrain says it contained unrest by individuals.

text.p: Bahrain said on Sunday it had contained what it described as "attempts by some desperate individuals to disturb the country's security and stability".
The official news agency also quoted an unnamed government source as saying some media reports on these incidents were "exaggerated and far away from objectivity and truth".
He did not say when the disturbances broke out, but added that the "security situation in Bahrain was completely stable..."
Residents said there were some minor incidents on December 16, the day Bahrain celebrated its silver jubilee.
Around 27 people, including three policemen and seven Bangladeshi workers, have been killed in two years of sporadic unrest by members of Bahrain's Shi'ite Moslem majority.
Some Shi'ite Moslems are seeking political and economic reforms from the country's Sunni rulers, including restoration of parliament dissolved in 1975 and the lifting of a ban on political parties.

Bahrain's ruler, Emir Sheikh Isa bin Sulman al-Khalifa, last week decreed the release of scores of prisoners including some held in connection with anti-government unrest. It still remains unclear when they will be freed.
